input.title: Delta Center Event Schedule and Downtown Parking Outlook: June 17-22, 2026
input.content:
# Delta Center Event Schedule & Parking Outlook, June 17–22, 2026 (for 328 W 200 S, Salt Lake City)

## TL;DR
- **The Delta Center has ZERO events from June 17–22, 2026** — the arena is dark for its summer "dual-sport" renovation, the Jazz/Mammoth seasons are over (the Utah Mammoth were eliminated from the playoffs by the Vegas Golden Knights, who won the series 4–2, clinching with a 5–1 Game 6 win at Delta Center on May 1, 2026), and the next scheduled event is Carín León on October 2, 2026. The Delta Center itself will NOT drive parking competition during Jason's visit.
- **One important correction:** "Vivint Smart Home Arena" and "EnergySolutions Arena" are former names of the Delta Center — the same building, not separate adjacent venues. There is no second arena to compound congestion.
- **The real parking pressure that week comes from non-arena sources:** the WBENC National Conference ("IMPACT," ~4,000+ attendees) at the Salt Palace June 15–18, the 50th annual Utah Arts Festival June 18–21 (across town at Library Square), and ordinary traffic at The Gateway directly across the street. Worst days near the home are Wednesday–Thursday, June 17–18; the week is otherwise relatively easy.

## Key Findings
1. **No Delta Center events June 17–22, 2026.** The official Delta Center events calendar lists nothing between the end of the NHL/NBA season and Carín León on October 2, 2026.
2. **The arena is under active summer construction.** Smith Entertainment Group (SEG) has the building in a roughly $525M renovation (part of a ~$900M downtown sports-and-entertainment district plan funded by a 0.5% sales tax over 30 years under 2024's SB272). Work is done in the NBA/NHL offseasons, with full completion expected in 2027. This summer's phase addresses the upper bowl, suites, new sideline "gondolas," and a new southwest-corner parking garage.
3. **No UFC, WWE, or concert in this window.** The 2026 UFC numbered event has been announced but no date set; WWE played the venue in fall 2025. UFC's prior Utah dates were in late summer/October.
4. **Adjacent venues are the Salt Palace (half block north) and The Gateway (directly across 200 South).** The Salt Palace hosts the WBENC National Conference June 15–18 (overlapping the window June 17–18), a small Robot Combat League event June 20–21, with the TGA Show starting June 23 (just after the window).
5. **The 50th annual Utah Arts Festival (June 18–21)** draws around 35,000 attendees (and reported more than 42,000 in 2025) but is at Library Square (200 E 400 S), about a mile east — it competes for downtown parking generally but not the immediate blocks around the home.
6. **Parking pricing near the Delta Center is much lower without an arena event.** Event-day lots typically run $10–$20; on non-event days hourly rates fall to roughly $1–$3/hour, with some lots (Triad Center, Gateway) offering cheap or free short-term options.

## Details

### 1. Delta Center — no events in the window
The official Delta Center calendar shows the next event after the season is **Carín León on October 2, 2026 at 8:00 pm**, followed by a string of October–November concerts (Disney Worlds Collide Oct 14, Kacey Musgraves Oct 15, Gorillaz Oct 20, Phoebe Bridgers Oct 21 [sold out], Smashing Pumpkins Oct 29, Dan + Shay Oct 30, Don Omar Nov 1, Teddy Swims Nov 3, Disney On Ice Nov 6–8). There is nothing listed for June 2026.

The reason is twofold:
- **The seasons are over.** The Utah Mammoth (NHL) were eliminated from the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs by the Vegas Golden Knights, who won the first-round series 4–2; Vegas clinched with a 5–1 win in Game 6 at the Delta Center on May 1, 2026 (Carolina ultimately won the Cup). The Utah Jazz (NBA) season also ended in spring. So there is no playoff hockey or basketball in June.
- **Summer renovation.** SEG has the building in the second phase of its multi-year transformation, with crews working on the upper bowl, suites, gondolas, and a new southwest-corner parking garage throughout the summer before the fall seasons. When complete, the project is slated to raise hockey capacity from about 11,131 to roughly 17,000 and basketball from about 18,206 to nearly 19,000.

### 2. Name confusion — one building, not several
The task references "Vivint Smart Home Arena area" and "EnergySolutions Arena" as if they were separate venues. They are not. The arena opened as the Delta Center (1991), was renamed EnergySolutions Arena (2006–2015), then Vivint Smart Home Arena / Vivint Arena (2015–2023), and reverted to Delta Center in 2023. **All four names refer to the single building at 301 W South Temple.** There is therefore no separate adjacent arena to add congestion.

### 3. UFC / WWE
TKO, the Utah Sports Commission, and SEG announced that a UFC numbered event will return to the Delta Center in 2026, but as of the most recent reporting **no date had been set**, and UFC's prior Salt Lake dates were in August–October (UFC 278 in 2022, UFC 291 in 2023, UFC 307 in Oct 2024). WWE's SmackDown and Saturday Night's Main Event ran the venue Oct 31–Nov 1, 2025. Neither falls in the June window.

### 4. Adjacent venues that DO matter for parking

**Salt Palace Convention Center (90–100 S West Temple, ~half block north of the home):**
- **WBENC National Conference ("IMPACT"), June 15–18, 2026 — ~4,000+ attendees.** WBENC's own exhibitor materials cite "approximately 4,000+ attendees." The conference overlaps the window on **June 17 and 18**, with daytime/Expo-floor activity at the Salt Palace (the venue's exhibitor-services contractor lists the Expo for June 17–18). This is the single biggest parking driver of the week and is very close to 328 W 200 S.
- **Robot Combat League National Championship, June 20–21** (Sat 10am–6pm, Sun 10am–4pm) — a small ticketed family event, likely well under 1,000 at a time. Minor impact.
- **TGA (Travel Goods Association) Show, June 23–25** — starts just after the window; June 22 is likely a move-in day with limited impact.

**The Gateway (400 W 200 S, directly across the street to the west):**
- An open-air shopping/dining/entertainment district with a Megaplex theater, restaurants, and summer programming (including a Salt Lake Gallery Stroll partnership on June 19 and kids' summer movies). It generates steady evening and weekend foot/vehicle traffic year-round, and its garages are the closest large structures to the home. Impact is moderate and constant rather than event-spiked.

**Utah Arts Festival (50th annual), June 18–21, at Library Square (200 E 400 S):**
- One of the longest-running and largest multidisciplinary arts festivals in the country, drawing around 35,000 attendees (more than 42,000 in 2025), with music headliners including GZA, Yola, Shakey Graves, Rubblebucket, and BANDALOOP. Hours are Thursday 5–11pm and Friday–Sunday noon–11pm. However, it is about a mile east of the home on the opposite side of downtown; organizers note downtown has 32,000+ parking spots and encourage transit. It tightens *overall* downtown parking, especially in the evenings, but should not directly fill the 300–400 W blocks.

### 5. Parking pricing — event vs. non-event
- **Delta Center event days (not applicable this week):** lots within a few blocks typically charge $10–$20, and some sources cite up to ~$20 within three blocks; the official box-office page lists surrounding lots at "$5 to $20."
- **Non-event days (what applies June 17–22):** hourly rates at downtown garages fall to roughly $1–$3/hour. The Triad Center offers about $2 for two hours; some Gateway lots offer free parking for the first hour. SpotHero advertises downtown SLC parking from about $7/day.
- **Net effect:** Because the Delta Center is dark, the event surge pricing that normally hits these lots will not occur. Garage parking around the home should be at baseline daily rates all week, except for modest weekday-daytime demand from the WBENC conference on June 17–18.

### 6. Street parking & residential permits
- 328 W 200 S sits in the downtown core. Salt Lake City runs a Residential Permit Parking Program ($51/year, prorated), with guest passes valid up to two days and visitor passes up to 30 days; eligibility depends on whether the specific block is signed as a permit area (look for area-numbered curb signs).
- On-street metered/time-limited parking applies on the surrounding blocks (200 S, 300 S, and the 300–400 W corridor). Standard city rules: 48/72-hour limits, red-bagged (reserved) meters cannot be used, and posted two-hour limits are enforced.
- With no arena event, the biggest street-parking competition will be **weekday daytime on June 17–18** (WBENC attendees and Gateway/Salt Palace workers) and **evenings/weekends** from Gateway patrons and Arts Festival spillover.

## Recommendations
1. **Plan around the calendar, not the arena.** Treat the Delta Center as a non-factor June 17–22. Don't pay "event parking" rates — there's no event, so any lot quoting $20+ is overcharging for this week.
2. **Expect the tightest competition Wednesday–Thursday, June 17–18 (daytime).** The WBENC conference (~4,000+) at the Salt Palace half a block north will fill nearby garages and some metered street spots during business hours. If Jason is arriving/unloading, aim for early morning or after ~6 pm those two days.
3. **Friday–Sunday (June 19–21): watch evenings.** The Gateway's weekend traffic plus Utah Arts Festival spillover will tighten things after ~5 pm, though the immediate 300–400 W blocks should stay manageable. The Robot Combat League at the Salt Palace (June 20–21) is minor.
4. **Monday, June 22 should be the easiest day** — no Salt Palace public event yet (TGA move-in), no arena event, lighter Gateway traffic.
5. **For a multi-day guest, the cheapest certain option is a reserved garage spot** via SpotHero/Parking.com at The Gateway or a 300 W garage (often well under $15/day with no event surcharge), rather than circling for metered street parking.
6. **If Jason will leave a car on the street for more than a day,** confirm whether the block is a residential-permit zone and, if so, get a 2-day guest pass from the city to avoid tickets; otherwise mind the 48/72-hour limits and meter hours.
7. **Benchmarks that would change this advice:** (a) A UFC date announcement landing in this window — currently not the case; check the Delta Center calendar before the visit. (b) Any late-added Salt Palace booking for June 19 or 22. (c) Confirmation that the WBENC conference's daytime hours run later than expected. Re-check the Delta Center and Visit Salt Lake calendars about a week before arrival.

## Caveats
- Event calendars can change; a concert or special event could theoretically be added on short notice, though the active renovation makes a June arena booking unlikely. Verify on deltacenter.com close to the date.
- The Salt Palace's official calendar is not machine-readable; the WBENC June 15–18 booking is confirmed via the venue's exhibitor-services contractor and WBENC's own site, and the ~4,000+ figure is WBENC's own estimate. For an authoritative day-by-day Salt Palace listing, call 385-468-2222.
- Specific lot prices fluctuate with demand and operator; treat the dollar figures as typical ranges, not guaranteed quotes.
- Whether 328 W 200 S is inside a signed residential-permit area should be verified on-site (look for area-numbered curb signs) or with SLC Transportation, since permit boundaries are block-specific.

# Free & Low-Cost Outdoor Fitness, Yoga & Social Workouts Near 328 W 200 S, Salt Lake City — Week of June 17–22, 2026

## TL;DR
- **The single best bets that actually fall within June 17–22 are on the weekend:** free Sunday-morning community yoga at the Hyatt Regency's Sundance Terrace ("NamaSTAY," 9 a.m., ~3 blocks away) and free "Yoga in the Park" at Jefferson Park (Sun 8–9 a.m.), plus the Downtown Farmers Market at Pioneer Park (Sat June 20, 8 a.m.–2 p.m., ~1 block away) as a social/movement anchor.
- **Both flagship events you named just miss the target week:** Salt Lake Power Yoga's "State of Mind — Yoga at the Capitol" does not begin its 2026 season until Wednesday June 24, and The Gateway's free "Sunset Yoga" runs on **Tuesdays** (June 16 and June 23 bracket your week, with nothing on June 17–22).
- **Weekday options within ~5 blocks are thinner and less certain:** the Gallivan Center's historic free "Weekday Workouts" series and the Main Library's free yoga are not confirmed on the public 2026 calendars for that specific week, so call ahead before showing up.

## Key Findings

**1. Yoga at the Utah State Capitol ("State of Mind") — recurring, free, but starts June 24 (just after your week).**
This is a well-established annual series organized by **Salt Lake Power Yoga (SLPY)**, led by Dillon Chase, held on the **south steps/lawn of the Utah State Capitol**, **Wednesdays at 7:00 p.m.**, and **free/donation-based** (community-funded). The Utah State Capitol's own events calendar confirms the first 2026 "State of Mind Yoga" date as **Wednesday, June 24** (listed verbatim as "State of Mind Yoga 2026 … Date: June 24," with 6:45 p.m. setup and 7:00 p.m. start). KUTV confirms the series "runs on Wednesdays at 7 p.m." and culminates in "Yoga Day in Utah" as the season finale (held Thursday, September 25, at 6:00 p.m. in 2025). **Bottom line: it does not run during June 17–22.** The closest session is June 24. No registration is required; bring a mat.

**2. The Gateway — yes, it runs free summer yoga, but on Tuesdays (misses your Wed–Mon window).**
The Gateway's free **"Sunset Yoga"** takes place at **Olympic Plaza (10 N Rio Grande St)**, **7:00 p.m.**, with the official 2026 Gateway calendar showing instances on **Tuesday June 2, Tuesday June 9, and Tuesday June 16** — i.e., a Tuesday-evening cadence running June through late August/early September. The class is **free**; per The Gateway's official Sunset Yoga calendar, "Beers available for purchase for $7 with valid ID," and there is live music from DJ Drew plus kombucha and wellness drinks for sale. Some past-season and press materials brand it as a Wednesday or "Yoga & Beer" event, so confirm the day. **Within June 17–22 there is no Gateway Sunset Yoga session** — the nearest are Tue June 16 (day before) and Tue June 23 (day after). The Gateway's published June calendar otherwise lists food, concerts, flea market and gallery events that week, not additional fitness programming. Reservations are encouraged ("space is limited") via The Gateway's website.

**3. Within ~1–5 blocks of 328 W 200 S during June 17–22:**
- **Downtown Farmers Market — Pioneer Park (350 W 300 S), ~1 block south. Saturday June 20, 8 a.m.–2 p.m.** Confirmed operating: per SLC.gov's Sustainability/Farmers Markets page, "Saturdays, June 6 – October 24, 2026, 8:00 AM – 2:00 PM at Historic Pioneer Park, 350 West 300 South." This is the state's largest farmers' market — it "attracts more than 10,000 people every weekend… accounting for approximately 60% of park visitations every year, per data collected by the Salt Lake City Downtown Alliance" (KSL.com, Feb. 27, 2026), a 300+ vendor market in its 33rd year. **Construction note:** Pioneer Park is mid-renovation — an **$18.4 million project** (KSL.com, Feb. 27, 2026; SLC.gov's release cites ~$18 million "funded through a combination of impact fees and voter-supported bond investments"). As a result, in 2026 the market operates as a "partial street affair": per Urban Markets director Carly Gillespie (KSL.com), "400 West would be temporarily closed from 300 South to 400 South, as would a portion of 300 South," and the market's own site confirms "Northbound traffic on 400 West will be closed during market hours." The market remains at Pioneer Park. A **"Free Yoga @ Downtown SLC Farmers Market"** event has existed in the past, but the **time, instructor, cost and whether it runs on June 20, 2026 could not be confirmed** — treat as unverified and check the market's channels or contact the market's program coordinator (blue@downtownslc.org).
- **Gallivan Center (239 S Main), ~5 blocks east — "Weekday Workouts" (historic, unconfirmed for 2026).** In prior summers this was a **free** Monday–Thursday series (yoga + bootcamp/circuit, ~5:15–5:30 p.m.) in partnership with the University of Utah's PEAK Health & Fitness program. **However, the Gallivan Center's public 2026 calendar does not currently list Weekday Workouts** for the week of June 17–22 (it shows food trucks, Dance Nights, Open Mic, and concerts that week). Verify directly before relying on it.
- **Salt Lake City Main Library / Library Square (210 E 400 S), ~5 blocks southeast.** The Library runs **free yoga led by Salt Lake Power Yoga instructors**, including indoor "Yoga at Main," a "Yoga with Jonnie" series (historically 1st & 3rd Thursdays), and summer **Rooftop Yoga** on the terrace. Specific June 17–22 dates/times are not confirmed on a single current page; check slcpl.org/events. Free; bring a mat; some sessions request RSVP/arriving early.

**4. Recurring free summer wellness programming in/near downtown parks during June 2026:**
- **SLC Public Lands "Yoga in the Park" — Jefferson Park (110 W Fremont Ave, ~1115 S). Sundays 8–9 a.m.** Confirmed by the SLC.gov events page: "Join us every Sunday, May through July, at Jefferson Park… Time: 8:00 a.m. – 9:00 a.m. Location: Jefferson Park, 110 W Fremont Ave (1115 S)… in collaboration with Full Circle Yoga." Free, no registration, all levels. **Sunday June 21 falls within your week.** (This is ~8–9 blocks south of the address, not within 3 blocks, but it is the city's flagship free outdoor yoga.) Note a source discrepancy: some third-party listings reference Pioneer Park, but the official 2026 city page specifies Jefferson Park.
- **SLC Public Lands "Pilates in the Park" — Donner Trail Park (2905 Kennedy Dr). Sundays 9–10 a.m., August–October.** Free, no registration. **Not in June and far east of downtown** — not relevant to your week.
- **"NamaSTAY @ the Hyatt" — Hyatt Regency Salt Lake City Sundance Terrace (~170 S West Temple), ~3 blocks east. Sunday mornings 9:00 a.m., late May–late September.** Free community yoga by Salt Lake Power Yoga. **Sunday June 21 falls within your week.** Open-air rooftop terrace; bring a mat.

**5. Run clubs / social workouts:**
- **lululemon City Creek Run Club** — meets at lululemon City Creek (~50 S Main), free, RSVP via Eventbrite, **4th Saturday monthly at 8 a.m.**, a ~3-mile run up Memory Grove/City Creek led by local runners Abby Warr and Grace Goddard with a post-run social. **In June 2026 the 4th Saturday is June 27 — just outside your week** (June 20 is the 3rd Saturday).
- **Salt Lake City Track Club** — free, noncompetitive weekly runs (Track Tuesday, Trail Thursday, Saturday Long Run, Sunday Stroll), open to all; non-members asked to sign a waiver if attending regularly. Some of these fall within June 17–22, but start locations vary and are not always downtown.
- **November Project** does **not** currently have an active Salt Lake City chapter (only a past pop-up and unfulfilled local interest), despite recurring requests — so it is not an option that week.

## Details

**Why the timing matters.** June 17, 2026 is a **Wednesday**; your window runs Wed June 17 through Mon June 22. The two highest-profile downtown outdoor yoga programs are calibrated to other days: the Capitol series is Wednesday-evenings but doesn't start until June 24, and The Gateway's is Tuesday-evenings (June 16 and June 23). The practical result is that **mid-week (Wed–Fri) free outdoor options immediately next to the address are limited**, while **the weekend (Sat–Sun) is rich**: the Saturday farmers market one block away, and two separate free Sunday-morning community yoga options (Hyatt Sundance Terrace and Jefferson Park).

**Cost summary.** All confirmed programs above are **free** (the Capitol and SLPY community classes are donation-supported; the Gateway class is free with optional $7 beers; library and Public Lands classes are free). The farmers market is free to enter.

**Registration.** Most are drop-in. The Gateway encourages reserving a spot online; lululemon requires an Eventbrite RSVP; library yoga sometimes requests RSVP and arriving 5–10 minutes early; Public Lands "Yoga in the Park" and "NamaSTAY" require no registration. Track Club asks regular participants to sign a waiver.

## Recommendations

1. **Anchor your week on the weekend.** For Sunday June 21, choose between **NamaSTAY @ the Hyatt (9 a.m., ~3 blocks)** or **Yoga in the Park at Jefferson Park (8–9 a.m.)** — both free, no signup. 2. **If you want the Capitol or Gateway experience specifically, extend by a day or two.** Catch **The Gateway Sunset Yoga on Tuesday June 23 (7 p.m.)** or the **Capitol "State of Mind" season opener on Wednesday June 24 (7 p.m.)** — both free and within easy walking distance.
3. **For weekday (Wed–Fri) movement, call ahead.** Phone the **Gallivan Center (801-535-6110)** to confirm whether free Weekday Workouts are running in 2026, and check **slcpl.org/events** for a library yoga session on Thursday June 18. - **Day-of-week conflicts are the central finding** and are based on the official 2026 calendars (Utah State Capitol; The Gateway). Both flagship programs fall just outside June 17–22.
- **The Gateway day-of-week** is listed as Tuesday on its official 2026 calendar but has been branded Wednesday/"Yoga & Beer" in some materials; confirm before going.
- **Gallivan "Weekday Workouts" and Main Library yoga for the specific week are unconfirmed** — historic patterns, not verified 2026 dates.
- **Farmers-market free yoga is unverified** for June 20, 2026 (the Facebook event exists but details weren't accessible); Pioneer Park is under construction, so layout differs and parts of 400 West/300 South are closed during market hours.
- **"Yoga in the Park" location** shows a Jefferson Park vs. Pioneer Park discrepancy across sources; the official city 2026 page says Jefferson Park (110 W Fremont Ave, ~1115 S), which is beyond a 3-block radius.

input.title: Summer 2026 Mountain Biking Lift Ticket Prices: Deer Valley, Park City Mountain, and Solitude
input.content:
# Summer 2026 Mountain Biking Lift Ticket Prices: Deer Valley, Park City Mountain & Solitude

## TL;DR
- **Deer Valley** is the cheapest and most transparent of the three: a full-day adult bike-park lift ticket is roughly $35 (child/senior ~$30), there is no true public half-day (afternoon tickets sell only bundled with a PM rental/lesson at 25% off the window rate), and the new Pedal Pass for riders not using the lifts is $12/day or $50/season.
- **Park City Mountain (PCMR)** charges from $53 online for an adult full-day bike-haul ticket ("Adult bike haul passes begin at $53 online," per Abode Park City), offers discounted after-5pm tickets at the window, and — importantly — no longer sells any summer/bike-haul season or multi-day pass for 2026, so every riding day is a separate day ticket.
- **Solitude** confirms a $25 Twilight bike-park ticket (Tuesdays *and* Thursdays, 4:00–8:00pm); its standard full-day day-ticket dollar figure is not published on accessible pages, but the resort advertises "up to 40%" savings for buying in advance versus the window.

## Key Findings
All three resorts price summer mountain-bike lift access far below winter ski tickets. Deer Valley and Solitude are Alterra/Ikon resorts and are deliberately cross-marketed (the joint Wasatch Gravity Pass covers both); Park City Mountain is a Vail/Epic resort whose Epic Pass explicitly does **not** include bike haul. For a week-long trip, the standout value is the **Wasatch Gravity Pass at $399**, which gives unlimited lift-served biking at both Deer Valley and Solitude all summer (Powder reports: "When it first launched in 2025, the pass was $450. This year, it's only $399," and Deer Valley's site confirms "Passes are just $399"). PCMR has no equivalent — there is no multi-day or season bike product there for 2026.

## Details

### 1. Deer Valley Resort (deervalley.com)
- **Season/operations:** Summer operations run June 19 – September 20, 2026. Bike-park lift access is via the Silver Lake Express, Sterling Express, and Homestake Express chairlifts.
- **Full-day adult bike ticket:** approximately $35 (the "all ages" adult rate); child and senior approximately $30. These are the most recently published Deer Valley Skier Services rates; the resort had not separately published confirmed standalone 2026 day-ticket dollar figures at the time of research, so they may differ slightly at checkout.
- **Half day:** Deer Valley does **not** sell a standard public afternoon-only bike ticket. An "Afternoon Bike Ticket" is offered at 25% off the window rate, but only in conjunction with a PM rental or lesson. There is therefore no general half-day walk-up option.
- **Online vs window:** Deer Valley limits the number of tickets sold daily and strongly encourages advance online purchase; tickets are retrieved via self-service kiosks at Snow Park and Silver Lake. Rates exclude sales tax.
- **Age-based pricing:** Adults 13–64; Senior 65+; Child 5–12; Tots 4 and under free with a paying adult. This summer, kids 12 and under also receive one free *scenic* lift ticket per paying adult. Deer Valley does not offer a separate student/teen rate.
- **Pedal Pass (new for 2026):** Required for all bike-park riders who are not using a lift ticket or season pass. It costs **$12 per day or $50 for the season**, per Deer Valley mountain-operations leadership (reported by TownLift), with revenue funding trail maintenance, bike patrol, operations, and guest safety in the lift-served park. The Pedal Pass is valid only during bike-park operating hours, 10am–6pm daily, including Twilight Wednesdays. All multi-use, multi-directional trails that do not connect to the bike park remain open and free to the public. (Context on why the fee was introduced: Deer Valley says lift-served trails typically cost around $100,000 per mile to build and about $150,000 a summer to maintain.)
- **Multi-day/season options:** Deer Valley Access Pass **$329** (full summer season, unlimited Deer Valley lift-served biking, hiking, and scenic rides; reduced from $425); Wasatch Gravity Pass **$399** (unlimited at both Deer Valley *and* Solitude — the best week-long value). Military discounts available. There is no fixed multi-day "3-day/5-day" bike ticket product publicized for summer; the season passes fill that role.

### 2. Park City Mountain Resort (parkcitymountain.com)
- **Season/operations:** Bike haul opens June 13, 2026 on the Crescent Lift (Park City Mountain Village) and the Red Pine Gondola (Canyons Village), running daily into September. Bike haul is **not** available on the PayDay or Town lifts (those run for scenic/hiking access only).
- **Full-day adult bike-haul ticket:** from **$53 online** ("Adult bike haul passes begin at $53 online," per Abode Park City / I Love Park City). The most recent resort/news-confirmed published figures were $49 adult / $35 child in summer 2023 (Park Record), so current pricing has risen modestly from there. PCMR's own storefront is a JavaScript page that did not expose a precise current adult figure during research.
- **Half day / twilight:** Discounted bike-haul day passes valid **only after 5pm** are available and are purchased at the Park City Mountain Village ticket windows (windows close 15 minutes before the resort closes). No published dollar figure for the after-5pm rate.
- **Online vs window:** Standard day tickets are sold online; the after-5pm discounted product is window-only.
- **Age-based pricing:** Children 4 and under ride free on scenic lifts. The child bike-haul rate was $35 in 2023; a precise 2026 child/youth/senior figure was not published on accessible pages.
- **Multi-day/season options:** **None.** Park City Mountain confirms (official Zendesk help center) that it does **not** offer a summer season pass for 2026; the former Bike Haul Season Pass ($220 adult / $110 child in 2023) has been discontinued. The Epic Pass does **not** include bike haul ("Bike haul not included with any Pass"). For a week-long trip, every PCMR riding day must be bought as a separate day ticket — making PCMR the most expensive option for frequent riders and the weakest fit for a multi-day plan.

### 3. Solitude Mountain Resort (solitudemountain.com)
- **Season/operations:** The bike park opens May 22, 2026. Lift access is via the Sunrise, Moonbeam Express, and Link chairlifts, generally 10am–6pm, with extended hours on Twilight nights.
- **Full-day adult bike-park ticket:** the exact dollar figure is not published on Solitude's accessible pages (the price lives in its JavaScript shop and the Ikon storefront). The resort's official bike-park page does confirm advance-purchase savings: "Book early to save 10% on lodging (excluding holidays) and up to 40% on lift tickets when you purchase in advance." A full-day ticket includes lift access and bike hauls on the Sunrise, Moonbeam Express, and Link chairs, conditions permitting.
- **Twilight ticket (confirmed):** **$25.** Per Solitude's official Twilight Nights page: "Ride Solitude's lift-served bike park for just $25 during Twilight Nights… Moonbeam Express, Sunrise, and Link lifts will operate until 8:00 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Tuesday Twilight Nights will run from June 16 through August 13." The covered hours are 4:00–8:00pm on both Tuesday and Thursday (the FAQ states "Twilight lift tickets include access to the Sunrise, Moonbeam Express, and Link lifts every Tuesday and Thursday from 4:00 PM - 8:00 PM"). Booking in advance saves money on the Twilight ticket too.
- **Half day:** No separate summer bike half-day product was identified (Solitude's "PM 1/2 Day" is a winter-ski-only ticket). The $25 Twilight ticket functions as the evening/partial-day option on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
- **Online vs window:** Advance online is cheaper than the window ("Save big by purchasing tickets in advance").
- **Age-based pricing:** Free scenic lift tickets are available at the window for guests ages 6 and under (Solitude's official Pre-Arrival Guide; a separate page lists "4 and under," but the Pre-Arrival Guide's "ages 6 and under" is the more detailed source). Helmets are required for all biking. Specific child/youth/senior bike-park day rates were not published on accessible pages.
- **Multi-day/season options:** Solitude Summer Pass **$299** (unlimited Solitude lift-served biking, hiking, and scenic rides; reduced from $350); standalone Solitude Bike Park Season Pass sold via Ikon (Solitude and Ikon pass holders save 25%; partner-resort Ikon add-on holders save 10%); and the joint Wasatch Gravity Pass **$399** covering both Solitude and Deer Valley — again the best week-long value if riding both.

## Recommendations
- **For a week-long trip riding both Deer Valley and Solitude:** Buy the **Wasatch Gravity Pass ($399)**. It covers unlimited lift-served biking at both resorts all summer and pays for itself in roughly 8–11 adult day-ticket equivalents — easily achieved on a week-long trip that mixes both mountains plus Twilight nights. Note it does **not** cover PCMR.
- **For Deer Valley only:** Riding 4+ days, the **Deer Valley Access Pass ($329)** beats day tickets. For 1–3 days, buy full-day tickets (~$35) online in advance. Add the $12/day Pedal Pass only if you plan to pedal the lift-served downhill trails without buying a lift ticket.
- **For Solitude only:** If riding several days plus Twilight nights, the **Solitude Summer Pass ($299)** is strong value. Otherwise buy day tickets online in advance and use the $25 Twilight tickets on Tuesday/Thursday evenings (4–8pm).
- **For PCMR:** Because there is no season or multi-day product, budget from ~$53/day per adult and buy online in advance; use the after-5pm discounted window ticket for short evening rides. If you'll ride PCMR several days in a week, this is the priciest plan of the three — consider shifting riding days to Deer Valley/Solitude under the Gravity Pass.
- **Thresholds that change the advice:** If Deer Valley's confirmed 2026 day rate lands materially above ~$40, the Access Pass break-even drops below 4 days. If you only ride PCMR's free town/multi-use trails (not lift-served), you need no ticket at all. If you're an Ikon Pass holder, factor in the 25% Solitude season-pass discount before buying day tickets.

## Caveats
- Live booking/shop pages for all three resorts are JavaScript storefronts that block automated retrieval, so several exact 2026 day-ticket dollar figures — Solitude's full-day adult rate, PCMR's precise current rate, and Deer Valley's confirmed-2026 standalone day rate — could not be verified directly and rely on the most recent published or aggregator figures. Confirm the exact number at checkout on each resort's official site.
- All prices exclude sales tax and are subject to change; resorts use dynamic and demand-based pricing.
- The $450 Wasatch Gravity Pass figure still appears on some legacy pages, but the confirmed 2026 price is $399 (reduced from the $450 launch price).
- Park City Mountain's "no summer season pass" status comes from its official help center (updated mid-2025); confirm it hasn't been reinstated for 2026 before assuming day tickets are the only option.
- Operating dates, lift availability, and Twilight schedules are weather- and conditions-dependent.
